transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Linda Kenyon.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky tells the BBC that he found it strange
that President Trump called Russian leader Volodymyr Putin a friend.
NPR's Joanna Kakissis reports from Kyiv that Zelensky also addressed the recent Ukrainian attack on a Russian warship.
Speaking to the BBC's Sarah Rainsford, Zelensky criticized Trump's friendly greeting of Putin at the recent trilateral summit in China.
Zelensky compared Putin to Adolf Hitler.
He's an aggressor and a killer. He can't be a friend.
It's the same that somebody say about Hitler during the Second World War that he's a good friend. No.
Meanwhile, Zelensky also said Ukraine had coordinated with nearby countries when Ukrainian sea drones attacked a Russian warship off the coast of Libya.
Italy's foreign minister, though, told local media that Italy, which is near Libya, was not informed.
Joanna Kakissis, NPR News, Kyiv.
Hundreds of thousands of customers are still without power today after a Thanksgiving storm swept across the east coast.
Rescue crews in New York City had to pull people from their flooded cars.
Amtrak canceled trains in Pennsylvania after a tree fell and blocked the tracks.
And King Tides bashed into the Pacific Coast, causing neighborhood flooding.
Felicia Combs is a meteorologist for The Weather Channel.
The coastal flooding with this storm was just, for lack of a better word, amazing.
The coastal erosion. Now, these are already a lot of coastal spots that were weakened by previous storms.
So we're kind of already behind the eight ball once this storm was beginning.
But the absolute inundation and the amount of flooding that I saw, of course, power can be restored.
It's horrible to not have power on Thanksgiving, and you hate to see that.
But when you're talking about roads washed out, whole neighborhoods flooding, that takes a little longer to get back from.
Combs says the double-digit inches of snowfall are possible along the mid-Mississippi Valley.
The U.K. government says it's investigating what it calls a serious cyber incident,
which forced it to take down nearly all of its online benefits and pension services.
NPR's Fatima Al-Qasab reports from London.
A government spokesperson said services were taken down as a precaution after unusual activity was detected.
And ministers say they're working with the National Cyber Security Center
and the Government Cyber Coordination Center to work out what happened.
The government has not ruled out the possibility that this was a hack,
but say there's currently no evidence that any personal data has been lost
or that a malicious actor has targeted any other government departments.
Officials say regular welfare and pension payments will be paid as normal,
but some Brits have reported not receiving their benefits as a result of the outage.
Fatima Al-Qasab, NPR News, London.
You're listening to NPR.
The U.S. Education Department has said it would spend $50 million in the coming years
to train aspiring and current teachers
to work with the country's growing population of people learning English.
NPR's Junaki Mehta reports.
This investment in English learners comes as a bit of a surprise.
Considering that last year, the Trump administration ended 28 grants aimed at English learners.
And when the department cut about half its staff,
almost everyone who worked on federal grants aimed at English learners was laid off.
At the time, the administration said the grants didn't align with its priorities.
Now it's funding 12 new grant projects that will help colleges partner with school districts
to provide training and support to new and existing teachers who work with English learners.
This is a big area of need as the number of students who are English learners in this country continues to rise.
Junaki Mehta, NPR News.
The Trump administration has given SpaceX the green light to deploy one million satellites,
it says, will be used to create data centers in space.
The Federal Communications Commission is promoting its authorization as an historic first
amid the artificial intelligence race.
Elon Musk, who owns SpaceX, welcomed the decision.
Musk has long vowed to create vast solar powered data centers in space to help run AI tools on Earth.
But scientists and industry experts have raised concerns about technical and financial obstacles,
as well as a host of other environmental issues that are associated with AI.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News in Washington.

topics.text: Zelensky criticizes Trump's friendly Putin greeting and compares Putin to Hitler
Ukraine says it coordinated with neighbors before sea drone attack on Russian warship off Libya
Italy says it was not informed about Ukraine's sea drone attack near Libya
Thanksgiving storm leaves hundreds of thousands without power and floods East Coast cities
Amtrak cancels Pennsylvania trains after fallen tree blocks tracks
King Tides flood neighborhoods along the Pacific Coast
UK investigates serious cyber incident that forced shutdown of government benefits and pension services
Education Department to spend $50 million training teachers of English learners
FCC authorizes SpaceX to deploy one million satellites for space-based data centers
